title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for the 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. The sheet is a scrap reused on the back of a typescript of SGA 7 exposé IX (Néron models, toric part of T_l). That explains the neighbouring 'pages', which are SGA 7 IX typescript and unrelated to this page.

Setting. S_k = k{T} is the divided-power (formal) power-series algebra over a ring k, with basis T^{(i)} and T^{(i)}T^{(j)} = binom(i+j,i) T^{(i+j)}. Ω_k is a group of transformations attached to S_k, defined on earlier pages. It contains two subgroups:
- G_k, presumably the automorphisms coming from PD-substitutions of the formal PD line;
- H_k, made of elements u_λ indexed by units λ of S_k (a 'twisting' or multiplicative part).

Computation. An element u_λ of H_k lies in G_k exactly when λT = T, i.e. (λ{T} − 1)T = 0. Write λ = Σ_{i≥0} λ_i T^{(i)} and use T^{(i)}·T = (i+1)T^{(i+1)}. Then
(λ − 1)T = (λ_0 − 1)T + Σ_{i≥1} (i+1) λ_i T^{(i+1)},
so the condition is λ_0 = 1 and (i+1)λ_i = 0 for all i ≥ 1.

Consequences.
- If k is torsion-free, λ = 1, so u_λ = id and G_k ∩ H_k is trivial. Conversely, if k has n-torsion for some n ≥ 2, take λ = 1 + a T^{(n−1)} with na = 0; this gives a nontrivial element. So 'and only in this case' is correct.
- In the torsion-free case G_k is also the full group G'_k = Aut(k{T}) of augmented k-algebra automorphisms. Reason: on a torsion-free ring a PD-structure is unique (γ_n(x) = x^n/n!), so every augmented automorphism is automatically a PD-automorphism.
- Hence (1 → H_k →) Ω_k → G'_k is split by G_k. Ω_k is the semidirect product of G_k ≅ G'_k by the kernel H_k.

General case. There is still an exact sequence 1 → H_k → Ω_k → G'_k = Aut_{k-alg augm.}(k{T}). The restriction G_k → G'_k has kernel G_k ∩ H_k ≅ {u_λ : λ = 1 + Σ_{i≥1} λ_i T^{(i)}, (i+1)λ_i = 0}, a torsion-dependent group. So the semidirect decomposition fails in the presence of torsion. This is the point being recorded: over Z or Z_p-type bases the symmetry group of the PD formal line carries extra torsion-supported automorphisms.
errors: No mathematical error in the displayed computation. If the marginal insertion really reads 'k sans tors. i.e. sur Q-alg', that identification is inaccurate: torsion-free does not mean Q-algebra (Z is torsion-free). But only torsion-freeness is used, so the argument is unaffected.
The precise definitions of Ω_k, G_k, H_k and u_λ are not on this page. The interpretation of G_k as PD-substitutions and H_k as multiplicative twists is inferred, not certain.

ideas.what: Computation of the units λ in the divided-power algebra k{T} with λT = T: the conditions λ_0 = 1 and (i+1)λ_i = 0, so the solutions are trivial iff k is torsion-free.
ideas.modern_name: Annihilator of T in the PD-polynomial algebra / torsion in the PD formal line

ideas.what: Extension 1 → H_k → Ω_k → Aut_{augm}(k{T}), split by G_k when k is torsion-free; the kernel G_k ∩ H_k measures the failure of splitting in general.
ideas.modern_name: Automorphism group of the formal PD line Ĝ_a^♯ / of the PD de Rham data, semidirect product decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in crystalline cohomology (Berthelot); much later Drinfeld / Bhatt–Lurie study of G_a^♯ and its automorphisms in prismatization

ideas.what: Uniqueness of PD-structures on torsion-free rings, giving Aut_PD = Aut_augm-alg of k{T}.
ideas.modern_name: Uniqueness of divided powers on Z-torsion-free rings

missed.claim: Grothendieck is studying the symmetry group of the formal divided-power line over an arbitrary base and isolates a torsion-supported kernel that breaks the semidirect product decomposition. This anticipates, in an elementary form, the role later played by automorphisms of G_a^♯ in Drinfeld's and Bhatt–Lurie's stacky approach to the PD/de Rham and prismatic theories. The link is only suggestive, since the definitions of Ω_k are not on this page.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical precedence for considering the automorphism group of the PD formal line as a structure group for PD de Rham complexes. The computation itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary but correct computation inside unpublished notes on the PD de Rham complex. It is mildly interesting as evidence that Grothendieck examined symmetry groups of the formal PD line in 1975–76, but contains no substantive new result.

The indexing set 'S_(k)' probably denotes units of S_k (S_k^×) or S(k); uncertain.
In the first diagram the kernel is written H'_k / H^f_k; later 'produit semi-direct de G_k ≃ G'_k et de H'_k'.
